name: Syngman Rhee
summary: Rhee championed Korean independence and sought reunification under the Republic of Korea. As president he pursued an alliance with the United States and backed land redistribution to tenant farmers. He used martial law and constitutional amendments to consolidate his presidency, and his government suppressed political opponents and the opposition press.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Rhee sought an enduring security pact with the United States and increased assistance to maintain and strengthen the South Korean armed forces.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Rhee praised the abolition of hereditary rank and condemned a system in which ancestry conferred authority regardless of individual ability.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Rhee championed land redistribution into the private ownership of tenant farmers.

class-collaboration.rationale: At the founding of the Republic, Rhee argued that labour, commerce and industry had to work together and called for national cooperation in place of conflict between classes.

collective-defense.rationale: Rhee insisted on a mutual defense pact, which committed each government to act on an armed attack covered by the treaty.

collective-farming.rationale: Rhee backed a land reform that established individually owned small farms through purchases by former tenants.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rhee defended the constitution as the product of deliberation by the National Assembly elected in the May 1948 general election.

death-penalty.rationale: Rhee’s government carried out the death sentence against Progressive Party leader Cho Bong-am on charges involving espionage.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rhee ordered the release of anti-communist prisoners to disrupt the armistice negotiations and pressed for the struggle to unify Korea to continue.

democracy-best.rationale: Facing a legislature unlikely to re-elect him in 1952, Rhee used martial law and arrests to compel a new method of presidential selection.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rhee forced through the 1952 amendment shifting selection of the president from the National Assembly to a popular election.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rhee’s constitutional amendment required voters to elect the president and vice-president directly.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: During the Korean War Rhee imposed martial law and arrested legislators amid his claims of an internal subversive plot.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Rhee pressed Washington for a mutual defense pact and obtained a treaty of indefinite duration with the United States.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rhee called for the same legal protection and opportunities across social ranks, singling out farmers and labourers previously denied them.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Rhee urged Koreans to mine and burn domestic coal and peat in place of cutting trees for household fuel.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rhee acted to obstruct the armistice negotiations because a truce would leave Korea divided.

future-generations.rationale: Rhee urged protection of soil and forests from erosion, asking how those who came after would live if farming left only rocks and sand.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No recorded position found on who should hold effective command outside the wartime and transitional arrangements.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rhee supported agrarian reform that broke up large estates and transferred the land to the people who worked it, with payments to the former owners.

leader-cult.rationale: In 1956 Rhee erected a bronze statue of himself on the former Chosen Shrine site, incorporating his own image into a public space devoted to Korean nationalism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rhee erected a public statue in 1959 honoring An Jung-geun, the independence activist executed by Japanese authorities.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Rhee called for an offensive against Communist China in his 1954 address to the United States Congress.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rhee’s administration made Christmas a national holiday, supported Christian broadcasting, and introduced military and prison chaplaincies.

national-resource-control.rationale: Rhee proclaimed South Korean maritime jurisdiction in 1952 to protect coastal fishing and other offshore resources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rhee pursued agrarian redistribution and kept monopolies in tobacco, salt and ginseng under state control.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The defense alliance Rhee secured explicitly granted the United States the right, by mutual agreement, to station land, air and naval forces in and around South Korea.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Rhee relied on the governing Liberal Party to preserve his hold on the presidency through constitutional revision and restrictions on opposition campaigning.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rhee used martial law and arrests to force the National Assembly to accept changes to the constitution that it had resisted.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rhee’s government kept the opposition daily Kyonghyang Sinmun shut after an initial court decision gave it an opportunity to reopen the paper.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rhee declared that improving the living conditions of struggling urban and rural workers was his new government’s foremost domestic concern.

profit-exploitation.rationale: No recorded position found on whether profit from ownership generally comes from worker exploitation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rhee backed compulsory subdivision and redistribution of large estates to tenants, with compensation for the previous owners.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Rhee ordered the release of prisoners in defiance of the armistice negotiations that threatened to leave Korea divided.

second-chamber.rationale: Rhee’s 1952 constitutional amendment introduced provision for a bicameral legislature.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rhee’s administration supported Protestant broadcasting and organized chaplaincies in public institutions.

separated-powers.rationale: Rhee used police coercion and wartime martial law against the Assembly to secure constitutional changes opposed by legislators.

state-harmful.rationale: Rhee led the Republic of Korea and used the presidency to build its governing and military institutions.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Rhee secured an indefinite alliance with the United States during the Cold War.

strong-leader.rationale: Rhee used martial law and the arrest of legislators to break the Assembly’s resistance to his 1952 constitutional amendment.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Rhee used martial law against legislators opposed to his constitutional changes. His government later kept an opposition newspaper closed and executed Progressive Party leader Cho Bong-am.

term-limits.rationale: Rhee secured an exemption from the presidential term limit that allowed him to continue seeking re-election.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rhee secured a constitutional revision in 1954 exempting the incumbent first president from the two-term limit.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rhee backed the land reform that broke up large estates and transferred plots into the hands of tenant farmers as small owners.

notes: Reviewed the full statement list across economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means and globalism. Follow-up research focused on agrarian and industrial policy, the constitutional crises and opposition repression, religion in public institutions, the Korean armistice and alliance, fishing and forest protection, nuclear research and early diplomatic writings. The research reactor evidence concerns research, while the nuclear power plant planning identified in the records began after his presidency.
